rows.col_1: POST https://developer.api.autodesk.com/construction/rfis/v3/projects/:projectId/search:rfis
User context required
data:read
JSON

Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow.
The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified as three-legged because it preserves user context.
Must be application/json

The ID of the project.
Use the Data Management API to retrieve the project ID. For more information, see the Retrieve a Project ID tutorial. You need to convert the project ID into a project ID for the Forma API by removing the “b." prefix. For example, a project ID of b.a4be0c34a-4ab7 translates to a project ID of a4be0c34a-4ab7.
The number of RFIs to return. Default: 10. Maximum: 200.
The number of items to skip before starting the result set. Default: 0.
Searches for a string in the title, question, and officialResponse fields.
A list of sort rules to apply. Each item includes a field to sort by and the sort order.

The field to sort by.
Possible values: createdAt, status, dueDate, title, location, updatedAt, closedAt, costImpact, scheduleImpact, priority, discipline, category, reference, customIdentifier, customAttribute

The sort order.
Possible values: DESC, ASC
A set of optional filters to narrow the results. You can combine multiple filters.
Filter by RFI status. Possible values: draft, submitted, open, openRev1, openRev2, answered, answeredRev1, answeredManager, closed, void. Note that workflow types determine which statuses are used.
Filters RFIs by the official response status. Possible values: answered, unanswered.

true: include RFIs that are hidden from the user.
false: (default) exclude hidden RFIs from the results.

Filter RFIs assigned to specific users.
To find the ID call GET users/me and check user.id.

Filter RFIs by location using Location Breakdown Structure (LBS) node IDs.
To retrieve location IDs, call GET nodes.’

Filter RFIs created after a specific date or within a date range.
Format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sz..YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sz.

Filter RFIs updated after a specific date, or within a date range.
Format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sz..YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sz.

Filter RFIs by close date or date range.
Format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sz..YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sz.

Filter RFIs by the user who created them.
To find the ID call GET users/me and check user.id.”

Filter RFIs by due date or due date range.
Format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sz..YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sz.

Filter RFIs by cost impact value.
Possible values: Yes, No, Unknown. For example, filter[costImpact]=Yes’

Filter RFIs by schedule impact value.
Possible values**: Yes, No, Unknown. For example, filter[scheduleImpact]=Yes’

Filter RFIs by priority level.
Possible values: High, Normal, Low. For example, filter[priority]=High.’

Filter by a list of specific RFI IDs.
To find the RFI IDs call GET rfis and check results.id.

Filter RFIs by the external reference ID (e.g., model number or spec reference).
Max length: 20 characters.
Max length: 20

Filter RFIs by discipline.
Values depend on the project configuration. Examples include Architectural. For example, filter[discipline]=Architectural.
Possible values: Building Management System, Electrical Substation, Security, Audio Visual, Food Service, Fire Alarm, Power Systems, Design Systems Integrator, Signage, Pathways, Cabling, Networks, Distributed Antenna System, Lighting, Vertical Transportation, Roofing, Architectural, Civil/Site, Concrete, Electrical, Exterior Envelope, Fire Protection, Interior/Finishes, Landscaping, Masonry, Mechanical, Plumbing, Structural, Other, Unspecified.

Filter RFIs by category.
Categories are customizable per project. Examples include Constructability, Code Compliance. For example, filter[category]=Constructability.
Possible values: Code Compliance, Constructability, Design Coordination, Documentation Conflict, Documentation Incomplete, Field condition, Other, Unspecified.

Filter RFIs by custom attributes.
Provide a map of key-value pairs using attribute ID and selected value ID.
For example, fd9a1234-aaaa-4444-bbbb-8888aa77ee66: value-id-1.

Filter RFIs by RFI type ID.
RFI types are defined at the project level. Use UUIDs returned from the project configuration.

Specify which attributes to include in the response.
Use this to limit the response to only the fields you need.
For example, fields=id, title.
A list of RFIs

The list of RFIs.
The system-generated ID of the RFI.
The user-defined identifier of the RFI.
The title of the RFI.
The question submitted in the RFI.

The URN of the virtual folder created for the RFI.
This folder stores all attachments related to the RFI.
The virtualFolderUrn is required when uploading attachments to an RFI. See the Upload Attachment tutorial for more details.

The current status of the RFI. Available values depend on the RFI’s workflow type:

For single-reviewer workflows (US):

Possible values:
draft, submitted, open, answered, rejected, closed, void.

For multi-reviewer workflows (EMEA):

Possible values:
draft, submitted, openRev1 (manager), openRev2 (reviewers), answeredRev1, answeredManager, closed, void.
To determine the workflow type, call GET users/me and check the workflowType value.
For details on RFI workflows in the Forma UI, see About RFI  Workflows – Autodesk Help.

The previous status of the RFI, if one exists.
This field is omitted if the RFI has no prior status (e.g., when newly created).


For single-reviewer workflows (US):


Possible values:
draft, submitted, open, answered, rejected, closed, void.


For multi-reviewer workflows (EMEA):

Possible values:
draft, submitted, openRev1 (manager), openRev2 (reviewers), answeredRev1, answeredManager, closed, void.
To determine the workflow type, call GET users/me and check the workflowType value.
For details on RFI workflows in the Forma UI, see About RFI Workflows – Autodesk Help.

The workflow type assigned to the RFI, which determines the allowed status transitions and the review path.
Possible values:

US: Single-reviewer workflow
EU: Multi-reviewer workflow

This value affects how statuses like submitted, openRev1, or answeredManager behave.
For status definitions, see the status and previousStatus fields.
The list of users assigned to the RFI.

The Autodesk ID of the assigned user.
To find details about the user, call GET users.
To retrieve the list of available assignees, call GET rfi-types and check the manager and projectReviewer fields.
The type of assignee. Will always be user.

The Autodesk ID of the user designated as the RFI Manager.
To find details about the user, call GET users.

The Autodesk ID of the user designated as the Construction Manager for this RFI.
To find details about the user, call GET users.
The list of architect users associated with the RFI.
The type of architect. Will always be user.

The Autodesk ID of the architect.
To find details about the user, call GET users.
The list of users assigned to review the RFI before it is closed.
The type of reviewer. Will always be user.

The Autodesk ID of the reviewer.
To find details about the user, call GET users.
The date and time by which a response to the RFI is expected, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sZ).

The default text for the Location field when creating a new RFI.
Note that the API does not auto-populate this value.
Clients are responsible for applying the default if desired.
To retrieve the default value configured for this field, call GET rfi-types.
A list of predefined location IDs associated with the RFI, based on the project’s Location Breakdown Structure (LBS). To get more information about the locations, call GET nodes.
The number of comments associated with the RFI.

The text of the official response submitted for the RFI.
Always empty when creating an RFI.

The status of the official response to the RFI.
Possible values: unanswered, answered.
Always unanswered when creating an RFI.

The list of users who contributed to the official response.
Always empty when creating an RFI.
The type of actor. Will always be user.

The Autodesk ID of the user.
To find details about the user, call GET users.

true: the RFI Manager is allowed to edit the official response after submission.
false: editing the official response is disabled. (default).
The date and time when the RFI was officially responded to, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sZ).

The Autodesk ID of the user who submitted the official response to the RFI.
To find details about the user, call GET users.

The Autodesk ID of the user who created the RFI.
To find details about the user, call GET users.
The date and time when the RFI was created, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sZ).

The Autodesk ID of the user who last updated the RFI.
To find details about the user, call GET users.
The date and time when the RFI was last updated, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sZ).
The date and time when the RFI was closed, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sZ).

The Autodesk ID of the user who closed the RFI.
To find details about the user, call GET users.
The ID of the container.
The Autodesk ID of the project the RFI belongs to.
A suggested answer for the RFI, typically entered by the assignee before submission of the official response.
A list of reviewers assigned to the RFI. Each entry may represent a user, role, or company.

The Autodesk ID of the reviewer. The reviewer can be a user (autodeskId), role (memberGroupId), or company (memberGroupId).
To find details about users, call GET users, to find details about companies, call GET companies.
Note that we do not currently support finding details about roles for a project.

The type of reviewer.
Possible values: user, role, company
A list of watchers who are notified about changes to the RFI. Each entry may represent a user, role, or company.

The Autodesk ID of the assigned user.
To find details about the user, call GET users.
To retrieve the list of available assignees, call GET rfi-types and check the manager and projectReviewer fields.

The type of watcher.
Possible values: user, role, company

The date and time when the official response to the RFI was submitted, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sZ).
Empty when creating an RFI.

The Autodesk ID of the user who submitted the official response to the RFI.
To find details about the user, call GET users.
Empty when creating an RFI.

The default cost impact value for new RFIs of this type.
Possible values: null, Yes, No, Unknown.
To check whether cost impact options are enabled and to retrieve the default value, call GET rfi-types.

The default schedule impact value for new RFIs of this type.
Possible values: null, Yes, No, Unknown.
To verify whether schedule impact tracking is enabled for the project and what the default value is, call GET rfi-types.

The default priority for new RFIs of this type.
The available priority values are configured in Project Admin.
If no default is set, this field is null.
Note that the API does not auto-populate this value when creating an RFI.
Clients are responsible for applying the default if desired.
The valid priority options can be retrieved by calling GET rfi-types <en/docs/acc/v1/reference/http/rfis-RFI-types-GET/>_. Some possible values: ``null`, High, Normal, Low.

The discipline associated with the RFI. To retrieve the supported values for the current project, call GET rfi-types.
Some possible values: Building Management System, Electrical Substation, Security, Audio Visual, Food Service, Fire Alarm, Power Systems, Design Systems Integrator, Signage, Pathways, Cabling, Networks, Distributed Antenna System, Lighting, Vertical Transportation, Roofing, Architectural, Civil/Site, Concrete, Electrical, Exterior Envelope, Fire Protection, Interior/Finishes, Landscaping, Masonry, Mechanical, Plumbing, Structural, Other.’

A list of predefined categories to assign to the RFI.
Categories help group RFIs for filtering and reporting. Each value must match a category configured in the project’s RFI settings. Categories are case-sensitive and project-specific.
RFI categories are configured in Project Admin and may differ between projects. Call GET rfi-types to retrieve the allowed values for this field.
Some possible values: Code Compliance, Constructability, Design Coordination, Documentation Conflict, Documentation Incomplete, Field condition, Other.
